author: José Olivares
description:
New Jersey congresswoman, charged with interfering with immigration arrest, set to face trial over May 2025 incident

An appeals court decided on Thursday that Democratic New Jersey representative LaMonica McIver will continue to face charges related to a skirmish outside an immigration detention center last year when she attempted to conduct an oversight visit there.

The court’s decision to decline McIver’s request to overturn the court’s earlier ruling comes just a day after she pressed the homeland security secretary for the Trump administration’s aggressive immigration enforcement operations, telling the secretary: “You are killing people.”

Continue reading...
title: Appeals court rejects Democrat LaMonica McIver’s bid to toss charges over ICE protest

author: Auzzy Byrdsell in New York and Lisa Bonos in San Francisco
description:
Anti-AI groups gather in front of Nasdaq exchange in Times Square and Anthropic’s headquarters in San Francisco

As the artificial intelligence startup Anthropic debuted on the US stock market at an eye-popping $2tn valuation Thursday, protesters from anti-AI groups rallied in front of the Nasdaq exchange at its New York City headquarters in Times Square and several were arrested. Similar demonstrations took place outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters.

“I think people are starting to get that there’s something wrong,” Jose Gonzalez, 46, one of roughly 30 protesters in New York City, said. Protesters carried flags reading “STOP TECH OLIGARCHS” and “FREEZE AI: END ICE, END WAR”.

Continue reading...
title: Protesters rally against Anthropic in New York and San Francisco after $2tn stock market debut

author: Associated Press
description:
More than a dozen people allegedly targeted trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear and other goods

More than a dozen people were charged on Thursday with allegedly orchestrating a vast train heist operation to steal more than $22m in cargo – from popular shoes to power tools – from major retailers.

A federal indictment unsealed on Thursday paints a picture of an organized group that targeted more than three dozen trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear, power tools and other consumer goods that were imported into the United States through Los Angeles and Long Beach, which are home to the busiest ports in the country.

Continue reading...
title: Suspects charged in California train heist ring that netted cargo worth $22m

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Measure fails 48-51 with GOP members again defending war that played a role in costing them midterm elections

The Senate on Thursday rejected a war powers resolution aimed at forcing Donald Trump to halt fighting with Iran, with Republicans once again defending a conflict that played a major role in their sweeping midterm election losses.

The House of Representatives had approved the resolution in September, and it was the first to be voted on by either chamber since the 3 November vote in which the GOP lost control of both chambers of Congress beginning next year.

Continue reading...
title: Senate Republicans rejects war powers bill to halt fighting in Iran

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Outgoing senator withheld ‘blue slip’ from T Elliot Gaiser, blocking his appointment to northern Texas district court

An outgoing Republican senator blocked one of Donald Trump’s judicial nominations on Wednesday, throwing a wrench in the party’s plans to approve the US president’s picks before Democrats take control of Congress.

John Cornyn of Texas, who is leaving the US Senate after nearly 24 years following his primary loss to a Trump-backed challenger, told the Associated Press he would not support T E
title: John Cornyn blocks Trump judicial nominee after Senate shouting match with Ted Cruz

author: Reuters
description:
Federal court rules providers can acknowledge gender identity and provide gender-affirming care

The Trump administration cannot impose restrictions barring healthcare providers that receive certain federal HIV-treatment ⁠funds from acknowledging the gender identity ⁠of their transgender patients ​or from providing them with gender-affirming care, a federal judge ruled on Thursday.

US district judge William Young in Boston sided with a group of national HIV medical associations and ⁠healthcare providers that challenged grant funding conditions imposed by the administration last year after Trump signed an executive order prohibiting federal funding for what he calls “gender ideology”.

Continue reading...
title: Judge bans Trump’s restrictions on HIV funds for transgender patients

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
The former Liberal MP had fought a long battle against glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Former Liberal MP Sharman Stone has died via voluntary assisted dying after spending much of her political career advocating that people should have autonomy over their bodies.

Stone died aged 75 on Wednesday surrounded by family after a long fight against glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer. She was minister for workforce participation from 2006-07.

Continue reading...
title: Howard-era minister Sharman Stone dies via voluntary assisted dying, aged 75

author: Rajeev Syal and Lisa O’Carroll
description:
Two sides to commit to discussing third-country hubs as part of reset pact after five-country deal with Rwanda

The UK and the EU plan to establish formal talks for the first time about sending rejected asylum seekers to third-country hubs, according to a leaked document.

A draft of a joint statement expected to be signed by Andy Burnham and Ursula von der Leyen at a summit on Friday morning states that both sides will establish “a structured dialogue” to discuss “returns to third countries”.

Continue reading...
title: UK and EU plan first talks on sending refused asylum seekers to third countries

author: Maya Yang
description:
Animal rights activists back the new law while workers’ unions oppose the ban over concerns about lost livelihoods

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, has signed a bill that will bring the city’s horse-drawn carriage industry to an end by 1 June 2028.

Known as Romanch’s Law, the legislation is named after 18-year-old Indian tourist, Romanch Mahajan, who was killed in June after being thrown from a carriage in Central Park when a horse became startled. The law marks the end of an industry that has operated in the city for more than a century.

Continue reading...
title: Mamdani signs bill to ban horse-drawn carriages in New York City

author: John Crace
description:
Old-school Tory with a heart wants to make London fun again – just don’t mention Brexit

  • Tories select James Cleverly as candidate for London mayor

Sooner or later, Sadiq Khan’s luck was bound to run out. Or was it? When he first stood for London mayor in 2016, the Tory candidate was Zac Goldsmith, who was accused of running a racist campaign. Not the brightest move in one of the most multicultural cities in Europe. Not to be outdone, four years later the Conservatives chose the completely anonymous Shaun Bailey. Even Shaun wasn’t sure who Shaun was. Especially when he was quite sure he could have sworn he wasn’t the Shaun Bailey who had an apparent Christmas party during lockdown, which he said “turned into something once I left
title: Jimmy Dimly is back and we should treasure him while we can | John Crace

author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey; produced by Annie La Vespa; music by Axel Kacoutié; executive producer Maz Ebtehaj
description:
Andy Burnham is meeting western leaders in Berlin and Brussels this week, to discuss Ukraine and closer ties to the EU. Meanwhile, Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have met at the Apec summit in China. Is this the start of a global shift of power away from Europe, or was it just a hyped-up photo opportunity?

You can read Pippa Crerar’s article on the EU’s approach to a reset with the UK here

Continue reading...
title: Is Europe now in the shadow of a Trump, Putin and Xi alliance? – podcast

author: Associated Press
description:
Officials recommend that residents in path of expected toxic plume vacate area, and some schools will be closed

Plans by the US army to detonate about 5 tons of bomb-making chemicals that have become unusable and might explode if moved have residents in south-east Iowa worried that a cloud of lead dust could cause environmental contamination and health problems.

The detonation at the Iowa army ammunition plant is scheduled for Friday, and officials recommend that some residents in nearby Middletown begin vacating the area that morning. If they cannot leave their homes, they should stay inside and keep windows and doors closed.

Continue reading...
title: US army plan to detonate bomb-making chemicals has Iowa residents bracing for lead dust cloud

author: Auzzy Byrdsell
description:
Colonoscopy, ultrasound, Vibration plate and patience deployed 11 days after beloved beast ingested knitted hat

Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has undergone a colonoscopy amid efforts to remove a knitted hat which she swallowed after it fell into her enclosure.

With surgery too risky for a full-grown hippos like Fiona, who weighs in the region of 2,500 pounds (1,113kg), veterinarians tried an alternative method of getting the hat to pass through her system.

Continue reading...
title: US zoo staff monitor Fiona the hippo’s rear end for signs of hat she ate

author: Ariana Baio
description:
US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake

Donald Trump was, again, accused of falling asleep during a televised event, this time during the speech of the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in China.

The US president appeared to close his eyes for roughly 10 seconds on Thursday. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.

Continue reading...
title: Trump accused of falling asleep during Xi Jinping speech at Apec summit in China

author: Caroline Davies and agency
description:
EHRC chair says ‘misinformation’ about guidance issued after supreme court ruling has created ‘more anxiety’

The head of the UK’s equalities watchdog has urged people to “take the temperature down” on reaction to guidance issued on single-sex spaces.

Mary-Ann Stephenson, the chair of the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC), appearing before MSPs in Holyrood, said “misinformation” over the body’s guidance had created “more anxiety among people”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Take temperature down’ over guidance on single-sex spaces, head of UK equalities body urges

author: George Chidi in Atlanta
description:
Jamie Davis falls just short as Democrats across south wonder whether blue wave could have been even bigger

Democrats are celebrating after, with Mary Peltola’s victory in Alaska, they have officially secured 56 Senate seats after the midterm elections. But Jamie Davis, who lost an incredibly close election for a Senate seat in Louisiana and could have made it 57, told the Guardian it “stings to come close”.

In Louisiana, which has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 2008, Davis lost to the Republican congresswoman Julia Letlow 49.1% to 50.9%. He was about 25,000 votes short in a state that cast about 1.5m votes.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It stings to come close’: Louisiana Democrat’s narrow failure to make it 57 Senate seats

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Former Tory councillor advertised ex-wife on swinging websites and drugged and bound her for sex

Four men have been convicted of sexually assaulting and raping a woman at the invitation of her husband who had drugged and bound her.

Philip Young, 50, advertised his then wife, Joanne Young, on dating and swinging websites, presenting it as a “kink” for both of them, Winchester crown court heard. In fact, he had been sedating her, plunging her into an “inanimate state” where anything could be done to her by whoever answered the adverts, jurors were told.

Continue reading...
title: Four UK men convicted of sexual assault and rape of woman at invitation of husband

author: Taz Ali
description:
Leaders focused on nuclear weapons and international court at their unprecedented gathering in Shenzhen

  • Apec summit live – latest updates

The presidents of the US, China and Russia met on Thursday for an unprecedented trilateral gathering on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen. The session lasted more than an hour and Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin touched on nuclear weapons, the war in Ukraine and wider international security.

The trio lead the world’s three major nuclear powers and their decisions have far-reaching consequences for global security. However, their meeting in China ended without an announced breakthrough or concrete agreement on the main issues. Here are five key takeaways:
title: ‘Really making history’: five takeaways from the meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin

author: Tom Perkins
description:
Natural Resources Defense Council shows how federal rules changes will increase public’s exposure to carcinogens

Amid a rise in early onset cancer, the Trump administration has taken more than 500 actions to systematically dismantle protections against carcinogens once in place across the federal government, an October report alleges.

The Natural Resources Defense Council report, and comments from current and former officials from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), brings into focus how myriad changes in federal rules or protocol will dramatically increase the public’s exposure to carcinogens. These are taking effect at a time when some forms of early onset cancer are s
title: Trump takes 500 actions to weaken cancer protections, new report says

author: Josh Butler
description:
Reported proposal to give musicians special treatment is ‘unworkable’, Aria CEO says, vowing to stand with other creatives

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The music industry will not accept an AI carveout deal that leaves other creative sectors behind, rejecting a reported proposal to give musicians special treatment while allowing big tech to train on other copyrighted material – described by David Pocock as a “divide and conquer strategy”.

The trade union representing writers and creatives is “alarmed” at a proposal to let AI companies train on Australian data if they buy a permit, an idea also strongly rebuffed by the Coalition and Greens.
title: Australian music industry rejects ‘divide and conquer’ proposal to give musicians exemption from AI scraping

author: Donna Lu Assistant editor, climate, environment and science
description:
Australian physicists chose to transmit the word ‘gravity’ in binary code through brick wall

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian scientists have used gravity as a means of communication, in a proof-of-concept experiment involving a snail-paced 1950s elevator, a brick wall and a men’s bathroom.

Physicists at the University of Queensland have used gravity to transmit a “practically unblockable” message about 70cm through a brick wall, by sending an elevator up and down between two floors and measuring changes in the gravitational field as a result of the movement.

Continue re
title: An elevator, a brick wall and a bathroom: scientists use gravity to send ‘practically unblockable’ message

author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
description:
Kristalina Georgieva says countries needed to be ready for tech rollout, adding: ‘You snooze, you lose’

  • Business live – latest updates

Booming demand for artificial intelligence will force the world’s most powerful central banks to raise interest rates, the head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned.

Kristalina Georgieva, the managing director of the Washington-based fund, said demand for AI hardware and related technology products was pushing up consumer prices around the world.

Continue reading...
title: AI demand will push up interest rates around the world, IMF head warns

author: Miranda Bryant Nordic correspondent
description:
Danish foreign minister says deal ‘removes all uncertainty’ over territory but warns trust in US needs rebuilding

  • Europe live – latest updates

The Danish parliament has unanimously approved a new Arctic security pact between Greenland, Denmark and the US in what it is hoped will mark a new chapter in relations, months after Donald Trump’s threats to invade the largely autonomous territory.

The deal, which was signed by the US president and the prime ministers of Greenland and Denmark, Jens-Frederik Nielsen and Mette Frederiksen, in September after months of talks, updates a 1951 defence agreement to give the US underwater access to Greenland and specific permission to construct a missile defence system.
title: Danish MPs approve Greenland security pact with US

author: Martin Belam
description:
The three leaders spoke about international peace and nuclear weapons as Trump hailed Putin as a ‘friend’. Plus, yes, GTA IV is really finally here, and the critics have their verdict – masterpiece

Good morning. Donald Trump has hailed his meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping by saying the three leaders were “really making history”. The trilateral meeting lasted roughly an hour and a half, according to Chinese state media. On arrival the US president described his Russian counterpart as “my friend”.

Putin told Xi and Trump that their countries shared “many converging interests” when it came to resolving conflicts, including the war in Ukraine, which the Russian president launched in 2022.

What was unusual about China’s welcome to the Japanese delegation? Apec’s Chinese hosts went out of their way to give world lead
title: First Thing: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic trilateral meeting in China

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Former NSW opposition leader warns party against becoming ‘Labor lite’ or ‘One Nation lite’ in late-night speech

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former New South Wales opposition leader, Mark Speakman, will not contest his seat at the March state election, the latest in a mass exodus of MPs under the Liberal leader who replaced him, Kellie Sloane.

In a late-night speech on Thursday, the final sitting day of NSW’s legislative assembly ahead of the vote, Speakman said he would not contest his south Sydney seat of Cronulla, which he has held since 2011.

Continue rea
title: Mark Speakman resigns and says Liberals face ‘existential threat’ as NSW exodus continues

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Stories revealing Pauline Hanson’s US trip with Gina Rinehart and the systematic betrayal of Kardell Lomas before her death recognised

Guardian Australia journalists have won two Walkley awards, one for a story about the systematic betrayal of a woman who was killed by her partner, and another for an exclusive story that revealed Pauline Hanson had travelled to the US with mining billionaire Gina Rinehart.

Investigative reporter Sarah Martin won the award for print/text news report for her exclusive story that revealed the One Nation leader and her chief of staff, James Ashby, travelled with Rinehart on the mining magnate’s Gulfstream 700 on 27 October last year.

Continue reading...<
title: Guardian Australia takes home two Walkley awards for excellence in journalism

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Democrats resoundingly nominated Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress is sworn in next year

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Hakeem Jeffries said it is the job of Democratic lawmakers to “fight Maga extremism” as he stood on the brink of becoming the first ever Black house speaker.

During a fiery House hearing, Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, defended his decision to take a government plane to attend a college football game, while thousands of flights had been cancelled and the airspace closed during the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) nationwide grounding over the weekend. “You want to bring up the fact that I took my family and my great nieces to an [Lousiana State University] game that was scheduled for weeks prior because I wanted to be a good uncle,” Mullin said, following questions from Congressman Bennie Thompson, the homeland security committee’s top Democr
title: Hakeem Jeffries on brink of Senate history as he tells Democrats to ‘fight Maga, not each other’ – US politics live

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
If the Aboriginal woman had been checked at regular intervals as required, her ‘excess consumption of water’ would have been prevented, inquest finds

• Warning: This article contains images of and references to Indigenous Australians who have died

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The death of an Aboriginal woman who collapsed after drinking at least 20 litres of water in a New South Wales prison cell was preventable and the result of systemic failures, a coroner has found.

Tammy Michelle Shipley, 47, died at Silverwater women’s correctional centre on 20 December 2022.
title: Tammy Shipley was supposed to be monitored in prison. Instead she died after drinking 20L of water

author: Tory Shepherd
description:
Inquest into deaths of four babies in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 told mother refused to give birth in hospital after hearing others’ traumatic stories

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Baby B’s mother was so determined to have a home birth she ignored the advice of experts – including her own midwife, an inquest has heard.

The inquest heard she was pregnant with twins, which she described as a “wonderful shock”, and didn’t want a hospital birth because she had heard of others’ traumatic experiences.

Continue reading...
title: Mother whose twin baby died was determined to have home birth despite advice of experts, NSW inquest hears

author: Petra Stock
description:
HMCS Spitfire commissioned by colonial government to protect against Russian warships based at Vladivostok during Crimean war

The wreck of Australia’s first locally-built warship has been discovered 128 years after sinking off the coast of far north Queensland.

Marine archaeologists found the remains of Ex HMCS Spitfire on 21 August, the anniversary of its sinking in 1898.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Remarkable luck’: wreck of first Australian-built warship discovered exactly 128 years after sinking

author: Cait Kelly
description:
Sports sections of British newspapers deliver their take on the unfolding Cricket Australia sandpaper saga

The sports sections of the UK’s major mastheads are relishing the never-ending crisis engulfing Australian cricketing, after a key player in the ball tampering controversy, Cameron Bancroft, alleged everyone on the team knew about the 2018 plot.

Bancroft’s allegation came five days after a lengthy media conference by the current Australia Test captain, Pat Cummins, during which he denied that everyone on the team was in on the sandpaper plan. Cummins was responding to the allegation first aired in team
title: ‘Shame old Aussies’ to ‘fresh chaos’: what the UK papers say about Bancroft’s explosive ball tampering claims

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Invoices, including for junior football and netball sponsorships totalling thousands of dollars, were part of ‘distorted’ payments to CFMEU official, inquiry told

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A labour hire company distorted payments, including to a former top CFMEU official, by creating fake invoices for sports club sponsorships worth thousands of dollars.

BK Labour Hire director Bernard Kearney continued his evidence to the royal commission into alleged corruption across Victoria’s construction sector on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’ll take the rap for that’: labour hire boss asked for fake invoices for sports club sponsorships, Big Build royal commission hears

author: Sarah Martin and Henry Belot
description:
Exclusive: Kelvin Morton was hired in February in appointment heralded as turning point for professionalisation of party

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation’s general manager, Kelvin Morton, has taken leave amid speculation that he will be sidelined from his role after a series of leaks about internal party processes and vetting scandals.

Morton’s leave, confirmed by several One Nation sources unauthorised to comment publicly, comes as the federal party finalises its pre-selection process for the federal election.

Si
title: One Nation’s general manager takes leave amid speculation he will be sidelined after leaks and vetting scandals

author: Catie McLeod and Jonathan Barrett
description:
Australian fashion chain becomes latest retailer in trouble after David Jones, Cue and Veronika Maine

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Youth fashion chain General Pants Co has become the latest major retailer to slide into voluntary administration, putting nearly 500 jobs at risk as Australia’s retail sector continues to struggle with cash-strapped shoppers and online-only competitors.

The collapse comes not long after that of upmarket department store David Jones and premium womenswear brands Cue and Veronika Maine, underscoring the mounting toll of tough economic conditions on established retailers.
title: General Pants Co enters voluntary administration, putting hundreds of jobs at risk

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Jobless rate rises from 4.7% to 4.9% for October, latest bureau of statistics figures reveal

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia may already have “one foot in recession” after unemployment surged to 4.9% in October, from 4.7%, in a shock increase that will add to rising worries this year’s five interest rate hikes have pushed the economy past a tipping point.

New figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed the number of employed people dropped by 43,500 in the month, confounding forecasts for jobs growth and a steady jobless rate.

Continue reading...
title: Australia may have ‘one foot in recession’ as unemployment surges to five-year high

author: Kat Wong
description:
Prosecutor argues accused could be convicted on strength of forensic and ballistics evidence alone in closing statement

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon’s claims about the deaths of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies are “fanciful in the extreme”, a court has heard.

The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon’s testimony about Jesse Baird and Luke Davies’ deaths ‘fanciful in the extreme’, crown alleges
